statusText: Tail rises to 22%. Mapped policy state: WATCH. A second failed retracement carried NQ Dec26 to a new session low of 31,196.75, with price 31,243.00 at 07:17Z, -0.51%, while Brent accelerated to 103.81, +3.60%. Repeated extension after failed retracements is genuine Tail evidence, but a 0.86% session range and a 15.08 VIX keep Tail below the 25% blocking threshold.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH with Tail at 22%, inside the 20-24% band and below the 25% blocking threshold. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers 12:30Z-15:00Z, spanning the jobless-claims print and the US cash open, where conditional Tail peaks at 23%. Conditional Tail returns to the EA_ON band from 19:00Z onward if intraday retracements of normal depth appear.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures extend to a second session low as crude accelerates above 103 and the long end holds near 24-year highs
body:
The eighth Globex hour of the Oct 7-8 session has extended the decline flagged an hour earlier rather than repairing it. NQ Dec26 trades 31,243.00 as of 07:17Z, -159.25 or -0.51% against a 31,402.25 prior close, with bid/ask at 31,236.50/31,237.25; a second independent quote put it at 31,240.75, -161.50 or -0.51%, so direction and magnitude are confirmed across sources. The prior hour's 31,313.50 low has been broken: price has extended to a new session low of 31,196.75 and trades about 46 points above it, inside the lower fifth of a 31,196.75-31,466.00 band worth 269.25 points or 0.86%. This is now the second failed retracement of the session, after the 05:16Z bounce to 31,409.75 also failed, so repeated extension after failed retracements is observed rather than inferred. That pattern is the specific amplifier the risk contract recognises, and it is why Tail moves from 14% to 22% and the mapped policy state to WATCH.

The cross-asset backdrop aligns with that tilt and has itself deteriorated within the hour. Brent trades 103.81, +3.61 or +3.60%, inside a 100.75-104.09 range, having accelerated from the +2.1% and 102.30 level reported in the Reuters Asian wrap and the +2.2% and 102.43 in the Associated Press version. The driver is verified supply risk rather than demand: UK Maritime Trade Operations recorded nine Strait of Hormuz attacks in October by Oct 7, about half of September's combined total, Gulf-to-China freight set a record near 1.3 million dollars a day, and Middle East export flows are estimated near 80% of pre-conflict levels. The long end remains the second channel: the 10-year is 5.30-5.31% after a 24-year high of 5.36% on Oct 7, the 30-year printed 5.73% intraday against a 5.64% H.15 fix for Oct 6, and the 2-year sits at 4.78-4.79%. September Fed minutes showed most members expecting another hike by year-end, with roughly 19% priced for October and 80% for December. AI-linked credit stress is the third channel, with SpaceX five-year CDS at a record near 197 basis points on Oct 7. Asian cash closed lower across the board, the Nikkei -0.9% to 69,438.77 and the Kospi -0.8% to 6,750.25, and the dollar index at 102.22 sits near an 18-month peak.

The counterweights are what keep this a WATCH rather than a block. The absolute magnitude is small: a 0.51% decline and a 0.86% session band are an orderly grind, not violent directional repricing. VIX closed at 15.08, so no volatility regime shift is priced, and price is holding 46 points off the low rather than pinned at the extreme. Cash NDX closed Oct 7 at 31,160.08 after a 30,904.46 low that was fully retraced into the close, which is the Oct 7 precedent for mean reversion still functioning in this regime. Oil, yields and event importance are treated as Stress and Confidence inputs under the standing contract until observed NQ structure establishes mean-reversion failure, so Stress rises to 58% while Tail stays inside the WATCH band. Confidence is 86%: current dual-sourced NQ and Brent quotes, a verified seven-day calendar and primary-source yields support it, while a stale VIX feed, an Oct 7 close on the 10-year quote page and unavailable shared Finviz context are the gaps. The shared Finviz evidence file was collected 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z with partial status, roughly nine days beyond the 90-minute freshness contract, so it was excluded and the assessment rests entirely on independent research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail ran 10-14% through the Asian and European hours of Oct 7, rose into a 20-23% WATCH band between 11:00Z and 15:00Z as a trend-down phase developed into the US cash open, then decayed steadily once the dip to 30,904.46 was fully retraced into the cash close. Every hour from 16:00Z through 05:00Z held the 10-18% EA_ON band, with Stress ranging 47-53%. The final lookback hour at 06:00Z marks the turn: Tail lifted to 14% and the mode flipped to trend-down as the 05:16Z retracement failed and price set a 31,313.50 low. That low has since been broken, which is the continuation this assessment prices.
outlookSummary: Base case is that the current downward grind resolves into two-way rotation during US cash hours, while firmer crude above 103, a long end near 24-year highs, a dollar index at an 18-month peak and AI-linked credit stress remain the dominant background conflict. Conditional Tail holds 22% through the European session and the 08:30Z Waller speech, eases to 21% into late morning, then peaks at 23% across the 12:30Z claims print and the 13:30Z US cash open, which is the published danger window. It returns to the EA_ON band from 19:00Z as the base case assumes orderly intraday price discovery, and settles at 13-16% through the overnight Globex and Asian hours. The 17:00Z 30-year auction is the day's most specific long-end transmission checkpoint. Confidence declines from 86% to 75% across the horizon because no current evidence constrains the later slots.
